# Tag tops in source bootstrap and unfollow subtree — analysis (generated by analyst on 2026-08-18)

## Problem

Two reachable tag-tree write/transition paths violate the intended v2 model. A source tag may be an existing top such as `tech`; after two tagger failures, the collector persists the source's unchanged `bootstrap_tags` into `post.tags`. Separately, `/unfollow-tag <top>` from `ALL` transitions to `EXPLICIT` but subtracts only the top's id from a seed made of leaf bootstrap names, leaving every descendant followed. The product decisions are rejection of tops for source/bootstrap tags, and subtree exclusion for a top unfollow.

## Ground truth

- `SourceUpsertService.upsert` rejects only names absent from `tag` before starting its transaction (`SourceUpsertService.java:250-254`); `unknownNodeTags` selects `name` with no `node_kind` restriction (`:277-304`). The subsequent source upsert stores the supplied array as `bootstrap_tags` (`:135-160`, `:257-260`).
- `AddSourceCommandHandler` catches that one exception and renders the existing localized fuzzy-suggestion reply without interpolating `unknownNames()` (`AddSourceCommandHandler.java:229-239`). This is consistent with M1-656's verified removal of raw tag echoes.
- `BootstrapLoader` currently accepts every existing node in `failFastOnNonNodeTags` (`BootstrapLoader.java:301-337`) and then writes the normalized array to `source.bootstrap_tags` (`:176-205`). Its pre-write fail-fast ordering and one aggregated operator error are already deliberate controls.
- After the second tagger failure, `TaggerWorker` returns `row.bootstrapTags()` (`TaggerWorker.java:463-478`) and `persistCursor` writes that returned list to `post.tags` in its atomic cursor update (`:710-731`). The prior M1-866 migration test verifies this fallback only with a migrated leaf (`TagTreeMigrationIT.java:370-394`); it does not protect a newly accepted top.
- `/get-tags` currently selects only `name`, alphabetically (`GetTagsCommandHandler.java:58-60`), and renders every entry with only a followed marker (`:132-140`), so it cannot explain which existing nodes are source-eligible.
- The ALL-to-EXPLICIT seed in `UnfollowTagCommandHandler` unnests `source.bootstrap_tags`, resolves each name to `tag`, and excludes `t.id <> ?` (`UnfollowTagCommandHandler.java:80-108`). The top's id is therefore never present when the array has leaves. `FollowTopDigestIT.unfollowSeedNodesFlowThroughExplicitDigest` currently covers leaf `ai`, not a top (`FollowTopDigestIT.java:187-223`).
- M1-865 established leaf-only tagger vocabulary and stored leaves; its review specifically falsified an assumption that a leaf-only source guard already existed. M1-866 established node membership, migration of historical bootstrap arrays, and a leaf-only fallback regression, but its approved review does not cover a top accepted after migration. M1-867 intentionally left the unfollow seed unchanged and pinned node-to-leaf read expansion; that is now superseded only for the ALL-to-EXPLICIT top subtraction.
- No listed red-team artifact exists. M1-489 requires shared trim/NFC/lowercase/character-class normalization for follow/unfollow; M1-656 requires friendly errors reachable below bot-admin not reflect inbound bytes.

The escalated M1-869 working-tree spec diff is not evidence of shipped behavior and is not adopted as the solution. Its claims conflict with the verified source and seed behavior above.

The intended contract for this analysis is now explicit: source and bootstrap
`bootstrap_tags` are references to existing leaf rows only. Top nodes remain
part of the controlled vocabulary for follow/filter semantics, but they are
not source-eligible and cannot reach the tagger fallback.

## Root cause

The source and bootstrap-loader gates prove *node membership*, while the fallback's storage boundary requires *leaf membership*. Because the fallback deliberately bypasses the tagger resolver, accepting a top at either source-input boundary makes a top persistable. The unfollow seed compares a leaf-derived row id with a requested top id rather than comparing the leaf's ancestor set; its one-row subtraction is correct only for leaf input.

## Pitfalls

- P1: A top reaches `post.tags` through the two-failure fallback, bypassing the resolver. This contradicts the leaf-only storage invariant from `docs/spec/schema.md §Sources and tags` and the tagger failure route in `docs/spec/security.md §Failure handling`.
- P2: Rejecting the chat command after a partial upsert, or letting the bootstrap loader write some sources before failing, breaks engineering-rules §10's validation/control preservation. The existing source gate is pre-transaction; the loader validates before its write work.
- P3: A restricted-dictionary reply that includes raw `tech` or other supplied bytes reopens M1-656's friendly-error reflection surface. Suggestions must come from trusted, normalized leaf rows and be localized in every bundle.
- P4: Presenting all tags identically in `/get-tags` leaves users unable to choose a valid source tag and makes P3's rejection inexplicable. The display distinction must not change follow semantics: tops remain valid follows and filters.
- P5: A seed that removes only the requested top id preserves its descendant leaves and defeats the user-facing exclusion. Conversely, changing read-time top expansion would break M1-867's future-leaf wildcard contract; only the transition seed changes.
- P6: New fixtures must describe the family end state. Bootstrap arrays used by the M1-883 test must be leaves, not a top merely to make the old SQL fail; the requested top belongs in the command argument and tree relation.
- P7: The top-unfollow path is adapter-inbound and must retain TagNormalizer, the DM/group authorization gate, scope isolation, tag-subscription version bump, and no-audit preference-mutation rule (engineering-rules §10; `docs/spec/security.md §Authorization model`).

## Solution options

1. Reject tops at both source/bootstrap input boundaries; list leaf suggestions and label the dictionary. This preserves leaf-only stored posts without inventing an arbitrary expansion choice. It implements `docs/spec/schema.md §Sources and tags`, `docs/spec/commands.md §Source management`, and `docs/spec/security.md §Failure handling`; risk is limited to two validation boundaries and their UI.
2. Expand a top to all descendant leaves at input. This avoids rejection but makes source configuration fan out, gives future leaf additions ambiguous source meaning, and changes the supplied bootstrap contract. Rejected by the user's explicit choice and by the smallest-write-boundary rule.
3. Keep the current ALL seed and clarify that top-unfollow retains the subtree. Rejected by the user's explicit subtree-exclusion choice and conflicts with the requested “everything except X” behavior.
4. Exclude the selected top and all descendants in the ALL-to-EXPLICIT SQL seed, retaining M1-867 read-time wildcard expansion. This is the chosen transition-only change; it implements `docs/spec/commands.md §Per-scope tag preferences` and preserves the D59 world predicate.

## Chosen approach

1. M1-882 changes the two source/bootstrap validation boundaries from “existing node” to “existing leaf”, carries normalized trusted leaf suggestions through a typed restricted-category result, and makes `/get-tags` visibly distinguish tops from source-eligible leaves. It preserves top eligibility for follows/search and the existing unknown-name path.
2. M1-883 changes only `INSERT_SEED_ALL_MINUS_ONE_SQL` so each source bootstrap leaf is omitted when it is the requested node or a descendant of it. It adds an end-to-end ALL-mode top-unfollow regression using leaf-valued source bootstrap data.
3. M1-884 follows both code tickets and records any remaining tag-tree contracts in discovery/help text. The leaf-only source/bootstrap contract is recorded in `schema.md`, `commands.md`, and `security.md` by M1-882; exact rule text was approved before this amendment under engineering-rules §12.

## Controls to preserve (engineering-rules §10)

- M1-882: `/add-source` URL probe and permission path remain before the upsert; source transaction atomicity, audit behavior for existing-admin replacement, normalized input, no-raw-input error rendering, bootstrap loader's aggregate pre-write fail-fast, and tagger's one atomic `post.tags` update stay unchanged.
- M1-883: authorization and group-admin checks, TagNormalizer, exact unknown-node fuzzy error, D59 world-source predicate, transaction/`FOR UPDATE` state transition, `tag_subscription_version` update, and no audit row for preferences remain unchanged.
- M1-884: no production behavior changes; localized bundle keys and command catalogue parity remain complete if documentation/help wording changes.

## Verification strategy

- P1/P2: `SourceUpsertServiceIT.topBootstrapTagIsRejectedWithoutWrites`, `BootstrapLoaderIT.topBootstrapTagFailsBeforeAnySourceWrite`, and a forced-two-failure `TaggerWorkerIT` regression whose source is loaded through `BootstrapLoader` prove no input route can persist a top and that the fallback consumes an admitted leaf-only source.
- P3/P4: an adapter-facing `/add-source --tags tech` test asserts a localized restricted-dictionary response with trusted leaf suggestions and no inbound token; `GetTagsCommandHandlerTest` asserts a distinct top/leaf render in every bundle/parity test.
- P5/P6: `FollowTopDigestIT.unfollowTopFromAllExcludesDescendantLeaves` seeds `ai` and `football`, invokes `/unfollow-tag tech`, and proves AI content and scope-tag rows are absent while the unrelated leaf remains.
- P7: existing normalization, authorization, no-audit, and leaf-unfollow tests stay green; the new top test observes the post-digest boundary, not merely the SQL result.

## Decomposition

- M1-882 — leaf-only source/bootstrap tags. It owns both write boundaries, the restricted-dictionary reply, and discoverability; it must land before a source can be trusted to contain leaves.
- M1-883 — subtree exclusion on ALL-to-EXPLICIT top unfollow. It is provider-only and independently verifiable but depends on M1-882's end-state fixture rule.
- M1-884 — tag-tree spec reconciliation. It depends on both behavior tickets so user-approved prose records reality. M1-882 and M1-883 share provider files and run sequentially; M1-884 is documentation-only after them.

## SPEC-GAP

Resolved by user-approved amendment. The existing tree/leaf storage and
deterministic bootstrap-fallback commitments support rejection and subtree
exclusion. Source/bootstrap input is leaf-only; top nodes remain legal only
for follow/filter operations. M1-884 is limited to any remaining discovery or
cross-ticket tag-tree reconciliation.
